data: Soviet / Russian heavy-lift workhorse 1967-2012 — Salyut, Mir, every Venera + Vega Venus probe, every Luna sample-return, and every Soviet outer-planet attempt

Three-stage hypergolic vehicle (N2O4 / UDMH) with optional Blok-D / D-1 / D-2 upper stages for high-energy escape missions. 311 launches 1967-03-10 (Proton-K with Soyuz 7K-L1 lunar capsule) through 2012-03-30, with a launch cadence that anchored Soviet planetary science (Venera 9-16, Vega 1/2, Mars-2/-3/-5/-7) and the entire Mir + ISS heavy-module deployment (Zarya, Zvezda, Pirs, Poisk, Rassvet). Replaced by Proton-M (still in service through 2025+); the K + M share the first three stages but differ in avionics + payload fairing options. The Blok-D upper stage was originally developed for the cancelled N1-L3 crewed lunar architecture; finding it a use case on Proton-K kept the heavy-energy Soviet planetary line alive into the 1980s.

The Soviet / Russian heavy-lift workhorse 1967-2012 — Salyut, Mir, Venera, Vega, Luna sample-return

Three-stage hypergolic (N2O4 / UDMH) heavy-lift vehicle with optional Blok-D / D-1 / D-2 high-energy upper stages. 311 launches between 1967-03-10 and 2012-03-30 — anchored every Salyut + Mir + ISS Russian-segment module, every Venera and Vega Venus probe, every Luna sample-return, and Soviet Mars-2/-3/-5/-7. The Blok-D upper stage was originally developed for the cancelled N1-L3 crewed lunar architecture; reusing it on Proton-K kept the heavy-energy Soviet planetary line viable into the 1980s. Replaced by Proton-M which still flies.
First robotic lunar sample return; first non-American lunar samples
First teleoperated rover to operate on another world
First spacecraft to soft-land on Mars
Second Soviet lunar rover; longest off-world drive (~39 km) for over 40 years
Last Soviet lunar mission; last uncrewed lunar landing for 37 years
Longest surface survival of any Venus mission (127 min); first colour panoramic images and first audio from another planet's surface
First-ever balloon aerostat deployed in another planet's atmosphere (Venus, 1985); first spacecraft to visit both a planet and a comet
First chemical analysis of Venusian highland-type soil (Aphrodite Terra, 1985); paired Halley encounter with Vega 1 fed Giotto's targeting solution
First wheeled vehicle to roam another world
First soft landing on Mars; 14.5 s of surface transmission
Roamed 39 km on the Moon — record till 2014
First colour images of the Venusian surface — survived 127 minutes in 457 °C / 89-atm conditions
Soviet Venus + Halley's Comet double mission — Venera lander, first interplanetary balloon, then Halley flyby
Sibling of Vega 1 — second Soviet Venus + Halley double mission, lander + balloon then Halley flyby
R-7-derived launcher for the first-generation Soyuz spacecraft — flew Soyuz 1 (1967) and Soyuz 11 (1971)
Soviet Moon rocket; four launches all failed
Vostok-K successor — more thrust for the heavier Voskhod capsule. Launched Voskhod 1 (1964) + Voskhod 2 (1965 Leonov EVA)
Soviet R-7-derived launcher that put Gagarin in space — Vostok 1 (1961-04-12) and 5 more Vostok flights through 1963
Carried Sputnik and Gagarin to orbit
Six hypergolic engines powered every Proton first stage
